extracted.intended_audience: newsroom leaders, journalists, media industry professionals, and readers interested in journalism ethics and AI
extracted.subtask_description: An investigative news report about an AI company's plagiarism on local news sites, and the resulting ethical, contractual, and editorial implications for newsrooms and vendors. The piece summarizes findings, reactions from clients, and lessons about AI use in journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper attribution when aggregating or republishing
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregators typically credit by name the reporters and outlets whose work they include; failing to credit sources is plagiarism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When collecting or summarizing reporting, explicitly name and credit original reporters and outlets. The article notes that Nota News republished content 'without attribution' and that aggregators 'typically credit by name the reporters and outlets whose work they include — something Rolz did not do.' Treat omission of bylines/credits as an anti-pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about the public status of experiments and projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies should be clear about whether an initiative is a public product or an internal experiment; contradictory messaging undermines trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The company called Nota News an 'experiment not meant to be seen by the public' while also promoting it via press releases and LinkedIn. Ensure public-facing statements match internal characterizations and that experiments are not surfaced to the public without disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear editorial guidelines and documented standards for contributors
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial roles and expectations must be defined in documentation; the absence of such guidance can enable ethical breaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contractors said 'there was no document that said what we were supposed to do or not'; organizations should provide concrete editorial policies, training, and oversight for staff and contractors to prevent improper practices like unattributed copying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human editorial oversight of AI-generated or AI-assisted output
rubrics_metrics.description: Human editors should review outputs from summarization or generation tools; some clients use AI only with human review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Institute for Nonprofit News 'uses Nota’s summarization technology' but 'Human editors review the output, and it does not use Nota’s article generation tool.' Best practice: limit AI to assistive tasks and require human review before publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit AI tool use to appropriate tasks (not full article generation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsrooms should restrict AI tools to tasks like SEO, headline suggestions, and metadata rather than using them to generate full reporting without oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boston Globe limited Nota usage to 'SEO, headline recommendations, related metadata, and social platform suggestions.' Outlets should define permitted uses and prohibit AI-generated news content being published under journalist bylines without disclosure and review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit consent and fair compensation for use of news content in model training
rubrics_metrics.description: AI companies should obtain permission and, where appropriate, compensation when using publishers' journalism to train models; the typical market practice is that AI firms pay news organizations for access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article contrasts Nota's claim that clients provided 'high quality journalism' for training with Meta's $150 million News Corp deal. Transparency about whether content was used for training and the terms (permission/payment) is expected by industry norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent statements about data usage and model training
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies must accurately disclose whether client data was used for training and how training was conducted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nota CEO asserted 'No data was used for model training' for the experiment. Organizations should give clear, verifiable explanations of training data sources and avoid contradictory or unverifiable claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible representation of client relationships and customer listings
rubrics_metrics.description: Vendors should accurately represent their clients; listing organizations as customers without agreement or after trials can be misleading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several outlets appeared on Nota's customers page despite not being ongoing clients or not authorizing training use. Best practice: obtain permission to display logos and keep customer lists current and accurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate mitigation and internal accountability when misconduct is discovered
rubrics_metrics.description: When plagiarism or ethical breaches occur, companies and newsrooms should take prompt corrective action, investigate, and communicate consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nota closed the project, fired contractors, and said it addressed the matter as an 'internal HR and management matter.' Effective responses include suspending services, investigating, terminating implicated staff if appropriate, and notifying affected parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not condition final payment on signing NDAs (labor and contract compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Employers or vendors should not withhold wages or require a nondisclosure agreement as a condition of receiving owed payment; this can violate labor laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nota asked a contractor to sign an NDA before processing her last invoice; experts called this 'very illegal.' Ensure contract and payment practices comply with employment and labor law and do not coerce NDAs to avoid accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable production expectations to prevent quality/ethics lapses
rubrics_metrics.description: Unrealistic demands for high-volume output (e.g., dozens of stories per week) can incentivize cutting ethical corners like unattributed copying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contractors were urged to produce 'upward of 80 stories a week,' which the article links to pressure that contributed to lapses. Set realistic workloads and prioritize quality and attribution over volume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Due diligence and evaluation when adopting vendor AI tools
rubrics_metrics.description: News organizations should evaluate vendor tools for efficiency, accuracy, and ethical risk before adopting them into workflows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several outlets trialed Nota and declined due to 'efficiency and accuracy concerns.' Perform trials, review accuracy, check data-handling practices, and consult legal/ethics teams before procurement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure to staff and pause of tool usage amid investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: If credible concerns surface about a vendor or tool, leadership should instruct staff to stop use while the organization reviews the relationship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Boston Globe instructed staff 'to stop using Nota products while it worked to end its contract with the company.' Prompt suspension limits further risk and buys time for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protecting reporters and outlets affected by vendor misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers and vendors should identify and notify journalists/outlets whose work was misused, and consider remediation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poynter's analysis found work from 'at least 53 journalists across 29 outlets' was used without attribution. Affected parties should be informed, and vendors should offer remediation or compensation where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency between public promotion and internal intent
rubrics_metrics.description: Promotional materials and public statements should not contradict internal claims about scope or intent of a project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marcaing and press releases promoting Nota News conflicted with the company's claim that the sites were not meant to be public. Avoid mixed messages that harm credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical limitations on AI-generated bylines and authorship claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals or organizations should not attribute authorship to people who did not originate or properly credit the underlying reporting and reporting sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contractors published stories 'under their own bylines' that contained copied reporting; ethical practice requires that bylines reflect true authorship and that AI-assisted content not be presented as original reporting when it largely reproduces others' work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain separation between assistive tools and core reporting responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Tools for summarization or metadata should not replace journalists' reporting duties; human reporters should remain responsible for news gathering and verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: INN uses Nota's summarization technology to help distribute members’ content but maintains human review; emphasize that assistive AI complements—not replaces—journalistic decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt external communication with clients and stakeholders about risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations that serve newsrooms should proactively inform clients and stakeholders of issues that may affect them (e.g., potential misuse of their content).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: INN 'shared Poynter’s story with members' to raise awareness. Vendors should notify clients swiftly if their content or data may have been affected and cooperate in assessments.
